- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments, especially after recent highs.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term mean reversion toward prior 10-15 day averages.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is rising — adjust downward by 1-2% for early forecast days.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high, don’t assume price will continue rising; model often overfits sentiment momentum.
